caption: The drawing is a technical illustration of a tall clock, labeled as "Tall Clock. Maple Inlaid." with specific dimensions and construction details. The clock is depicted in two main views: a front view on the left and a side view on the right. Each view shows the clock’s structural and decorative features in black ink lines on a beige background. The clock has a tall rectangular base (19 inches wide in front, 9⅞ inches deep from the side) and a narrower, elongated midsection, surmounted by an ornate, arched top with decorative finials labeled "Brass." The front view highlights details such as a pane of "Glass" in the arched upper section and a vertical "Door" with fluting on the central body. The side view includes a similar upper glass window and marks the "Brass cap and base." Dimensions are annotated, including the height to the wavy line at 41 inches from the base, the total central width as 15 inches, and full height as 100 inches. Additional elements include ornamental scrollwork at the top corners, moldings, and a scalloped motif along the base. Handwritten notations designate material (maple inlaid), parts (glass, flute, door), and scale (⅛ inch = 1 inch), along with the drafter's name, Isidore Sovensky. The style is precise and architectural, with straight and curved lines denoting structure and embellishment.
title: Tall Clock
